questions.question: How many kilograms of sugar at ₹3.80 per kg should be mixed with 60 kgs of sugar at ₹4.60 per kg, so that by selling the mixture at ₹5 per kg, there may be gain of 25%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 5 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹4 per kg.

By alligation, ratio of quantities = (4.60 − 4.00) : (4.00 − 3.80) = 0.60 : 0.20 = 3 : 1.

Let the required quantity of the first type of sugar be x kg.

x : 60 = 3 : 1 ⇒ x = 60 × 3 = 180 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of 1st type of sugar = ₹3.80 per kg

Quantity of 2nd type of sugar = 60 kg

Price of 2nd type of sugar = ₹4.60 per kg

Selling Price (SP) of mixture = ₹5 per kg

Gain percentage = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Gain%)]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 5 × [100 ÷ (100 + 25)] = 5 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹4 per kg

⇒ Let the required quantity of the first type of sugar be x kg.

⇒ Applying the rule of alligation:

•

 ₹4.60 (60 kg)
 
 Mean: ₹4.00

 Ratio → 3 : 1

⇒ From the alligation diagram, the ratio of quantities = 0.60 : 0.20 = 3 : 1

⇒ x ÷ 60 = 3 ÷ 1

⇒ x = 60 × 3

⇒ x = 180 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 180 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

It is a method used to find the exact ratio in which two ingredients at different prices must be mixed to get a mixture of a desired mean price. Ratio = (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Profit & Loss Base

Profit or Loss percentages are fundamentally calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the problem. If Selling Price (SP) is given, CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)].

Successive Replacement Method

If initially a vessel contains a liters of liquid, and b liters are withdrawn and replaced by water n times, the final quantity of pure liquid left = a × (1 − b ÷ a)ⁿ.

questions.question: To do a certain work, Q and R work on alternate days, with Q beginning the work on the first day. Q can finish the work alone in 56 days. If the work gets completed in 37.5 days, then R alone can finish half of the same work in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 37.5 days. Since Q starts the work, Q works for 19 days (all odd days up to 37) and R works for 18.5 days (all even days up to 36, plus 0.5 day on the 38th day).

Work done by Q = 19 ÷ 56.

Remaining work = 1 − (19 ÷ 56) = 37 ÷ 56.

R completes 37 ÷ 56 of the work in 18.5 days.

Time for R to complete the whole work = (18.5 × 56) ÷ 37 = 28 days.

Time for R to complete half of the work = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Q to finish the work = 56 days

Total time taken by Q and R working alternately = 37.5 days

Let the total work be 56 units (which is the LCM of 56).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total days = 37.5 days

⇒ Since Q starts, Q works on days 1, 3, 5, ..., 37 (total 19 days).

⇒ R works on days 2, 4, 6, ..., 36 and for 0.5 days on day 38 (total 18.5 days).

⇒ Work done by Q = 19 days × 1 unit/day = 19 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 56 − 19 = 37 units.

⇒ This remaining work is completed by R in 18.5 days.

⇒ Efficiency of R = 37 ÷ 18.5 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Time required by R alone to complete the full work = 56 ÷ 2 = 28 days.

⇒ Time required by R alone to complete half of the work = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work Cycle

When individuals work alternately, calculating the work done in one complete 2-day cycle simplifies the process of finding the total number of days taken.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken.

Fractional Work Calculation

If a person can complete a task in N days, the time taken to complete a fraction of the work is N × Fraction of work.

questions.question: The third proportional to 0.13 and 0.52 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The third proportional of two numbers a and b is given by b² ÷ a.

For finding it quickly, calculate the multiplier between the first and second term.

Multiplier = 0.52 ÷ 0.13 = 4

Third proportional = Second term × Multiplier = 0.52 × 4 = 2.08

**∴ The correct answer is 2.08.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 0.13

Second number (b) = 0.52

**Formula Used:**

If three terms a, b, and c are in continuous proportion, then a : b = b : c.

⇒ a ÷ b = b ÷ c

⇒ c = b² ÷ a

**Calculations:**

⇒ c = (0.52 × 0.52) ÷ 0.13

⇒ c = 0.52 × (0.52 ÷ 0.13)

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two given numbers a and b is √(a × b). It acts as the geometric mean.

Fourth Proportional

For three separate numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional x satisfies a : b :: c : x. It is calculated using the formula x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are combined by multiplying their corresponding antecedents and consequents term by term, it creates a compound ratio. For a : b and c : d, it is ac : bd.

questions.question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹486 for a period of 3 years at the rate of 8% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total effective interest rate for 3 years = 8% × 3 = 24%

According to the question, 24% of the Principal = ₹486

1% of the Principal = 486 ÷ 24 = ₹20.25

Principal (100%) = 20.25 × 100 = ₹2025

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2025.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹486

Rate of Interest (R) = 8% per annum

Time period (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Principal (P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

 
 Principal (P)
 ?
 

 8% per annum
 3 Years
 
 Simple Interest
 ₹486
 Total Interest % = 8% × 3 = 24%
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ P = (486 × 100) ÷ (8 × 3)

⇒ P = 48600 ÷ 24

⇒ P = ₹2025

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2025.**

**__Additional Information__**

Amount under Simple Interest

The total amount (A) after T years is the sum of the Principal and the Simple Interest. Formula: A = P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, if compounded annually, Simple Interest and Compound Interest remain exactly equal. From the second year onwards, Compound Interest is strictly greater than Simple Interest on the same principal amount.

Rule of 72

A commonly used financial shortcut to estimate how many years it will take to double an investment at a given interest rate (R) is approximately calculated as 72 ÷ R.

questions.question: The LCM of 18, 72, 184 and 144 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

144 is a direct multiple of both 18 and 72, so their combined LCM is simply 144.

We now only need to find the LCM of 144 and 184.

Extracting the highest common factor 8, we get: 144 = 8 × 18 and 184 = 8 × 23.

The LCM is the product of the common factor and the remaining uncommon factors.

LCM = 8 × 18 × 23 = 144 × 23 = 3312.

**∴ The correct answer is 3312.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 18, 72, 184, and 144.

**Method Used:**

The LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present in the given numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 184 = 2³ × 23

⇒ Prime factorization of 144 = 2⁴ × 3²

⇒ The highest power of 2 is 2⁴

⇒ The highest power of 3 is 3²

⇒ The highest power of 23 is 23¹

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3² × 23

⇒ LCM = 16 × 9 × 23

⇒ LCM = 144 × 23 = 3312

**∴ The correct answer is 3312.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their LCM and HCF is equal to the product of the numbers: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b.

LCM of Fractions

The LCM of two or more fractions is calculated as: LCM = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).

HCF of Fractions

The HCF of two or more fractions is calculated as: HCF = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators).

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (having no common factor other than 1), their HCF is 1 and their LCM is strictly equal to their product.

questions.question: The average weight of Chetan, Vipul and Mohan is 46 kg. If the average weight of Chetan and Vipul be 40 kg and that of Vipul and Mohan be 44 kg, then the weight of Vipul (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight of Chetan, Vipul and Mohan = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

Combined weight of (Chetan + Vipul) and (Vipul + Mohan) = (40 × 2) + (44 × 2) = 168 kg

Since Vipul's weight is counted twice in the above combined sum, we can find his exact weight by subtraction:

Weight of Vipul = 168 − 138 = 30 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 30 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Chetan, Vipul and Mohan = 46 kg

Average weight of Chetan and Vipul = 40 kg

Average weight of Vipul and Mohan = 44 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of persons

 
 

 Total (Chetan + Vipul + Mohan) = 138 kg

 
 

 Chetan + Vipul = 80 kg

 
 
 Chetan

 
 Vipul

 
 Mohan

 
 

 Vipul + Mohan = 88 kg

 
 

 Vipul = (80 + 88) − 138 = 30 kg

**Calculations:**

Let the weights of Chetan, Vipul, and Mohan be C, V, and M respectively.

⇒ Total weight of all three = C + V + M = 46 × 3 = 138 kg --- (1)

⇒ Total weight of Chetan and Vipul = C + V = 40 × 2 = 80 kg --- (2)

⇒ Total weight of Vipul and Mohan = V + M = 44 × 2 = 88 kg --- (3)

Adding equations (2) and (3):

⇒ (C + V) + (V + M) = 80 + 88

⇒ C + 2V + M = 168 kg --- (4)

Subtracting equation (1) from (4):

⇒ (C + 2V + M) − (C + V + M) = 168 − 138

⇒ V = 30 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 30 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average is mathematically defined as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Average = Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations.

Overlapping Groups Concept

When one individual or item is counted simultaneously in two separate sub-groups, the sum of those two sub-groups will strictly exceed the actual combined group total. The exact value of the overlapping item is determined by the difference between the sum of the sub-groups and the actual total sum.

Weighted Average

Used when dealing with multiple groups of different sample sizes. Formula: Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n represents the number of elements and A represents their respective averages.
</p

questions.question: There are three persons M,N And P. They are running in the same direction around a circular track of length 150 m. Their speeds are 20 m/sec,15 m/sec and 12 m/sec, respectively. If they start at same time and same point, then after what time do they meet for the first time?

questions.question: A medicine has 60% substance S and 40% substance T. If the cost price of S is increased from ₹30 to ₹40 per unit and the cost price of T is decreased to ₹20 from ₹30 per unit, then the cost of the medicine will _____ by _____%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change per unit = (Proportion of S × Change in S) + (Proportion of T × Change in T)

Net change = (60% × +10) + (40% × −10) = +6 − 4 = +₹2

Initial average cost per unit = (60% × 30) + (40% × 30) = ₹30

Percentage increase = (Net change ÷ Initial cost) × 100

Percentage increase = (2 ÷ 30) × 100 ≈ 6.67%

**∴ The correct answer is increase by 6.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Composition: Substance S = 60%, Substance T = 40%

Initial cost of S = ₹30/unit, Initial cost of T = ₹30/unit

questions.question: A store offers two successive discounts of 12% and 18% on an item. What is the equivalent single discount that a customer would receive if these two discounts were applied together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The equivalent single discount for two successive discounts of x% and y% is given by the formula: **x + y − (x × y ÷ 100)**

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 12 + 18 − (12 × 18 ÷ 100)

⇒ 30 − (216 ÷ 100)

⇒ 30 − 2.16 = 27.84%

**∴ The correct answer is 27.84%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First successive discount (D₁) = 12%

Second successive discount (D₂) = 18%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − D₁) ÷ 100 × (100 − D₂) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When a discount is given on an already discounted price, it is called a successive discount. The equivalent single discount for three successive discounts of x%, y%, and z% is calculated by first finding the equivalent of x% and y%, and then applying the formula again with z%.

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

A discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (also known as the List Price). The final Selling Price is derived by subtracting the discount from the Marked Price (SP = MP − Discount).

Net Change Formula

The overall percentage change for any two consecutive changes of A% and B% can be calculated using the net effect formula: A + B + (A × B ÷ 100). For discounts, the values of A and B are taken as negative quantities.
